observations.text: SP, due to an unstructured briefing method that did not follow the IFG/CRM matrix chart, did not identify the CRM items applicable to the sortie and left mission planning, communication and airmanship unaddressed in the brief. The same omission continued in flight, and the CRM concept was not used when the holding entry and the approach sequence were analyzed. The result was that the IP had to direct the division of cockpit duties and execute part of the radio work. The CRM box was completed only after the IP reconstructed the sortie during the debriefing.

SP, due to absent explicit role assignment when the unexpected re-route was issued, did not state who was flying and who was working the approach plate, and the CRM concept was not used to analyze the changed situation. Aircraft control, navigation and communication were attempted simultaneously in the rear cockpit. The result was that the IP had to take the radios and direct part of the approach setup before the aircraft could be established. SP could not identify the point at which coordination broke down without IP reconstruction in the debriefing.

SP integrated CRM skills into the briefing and the debriefing at the level required for the Training Section, although the IFG/CRM matrix chart was used only after the IP's verbal indications and the applicable items were highlighted with delay. In flight the division of radio and navigation duties was established after prompting rather than on SP's own initiative. Performance is at the desired standard but marginal, since verbal indications were required at each phase change. Independent use of the matrix chart and earlier statement of cockpit duties are expected to improve over the next sorties.

SP briefed the applicable CRM items from the IFG/CRM matrix chart without prompting and stated the division of cockpit duties before departure. Minor errors occurred in that the workload was not rebalanced immediately when the approach clearance changed, but SP recognized this and reallocated the radio and navigation tasks in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Particular areas for CRM development were identified by SP during the debriefing. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP integrated CRM skills accurately and rapidly into the briefing, the flight and the debriefing, highlighting the applicable items on the IFG/CRM matrix chart on his own initiative. The CRM concept was applied when the holding entry and the alternate approach were planned, with standard and timely communication between cockpits throughout. SP demonstrated understanding of when CRM enhances mission performance and flight safety and solicited comments on it during the debriefing. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional CRM throughout the instrument sortie, briefing the applicable matrix chart items together with the identified threats and stating the divert criteria and the named decision points before engine start. Under the increased workload of the unplanned approach change, the explicit role assignment, the inquiry toward the IP and the plain-language statement of intentions to ATC were all maintained without degradation. In the debriefing SP identified his own areas for CRM development and the points at which crew coordination enhanced mission effectiveness and safety. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a briefing technique that treated the IFG/CRM matrix chart as a checkbox rather than as a tool for highlighting particular items, did not brief the CRM items applicable to the instrument sortie and agreed no division of cockpit duties for the approach phase. When the approach was changed in flight, the CRM concept was not used to analyze the new situation. The result was that the IP had to direct the sequence and execute the radio work and the navigation setup. Study of the CRM briefing content is required before the next instrument sortie.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in stating unable when the clearance could not be complied with, did not communicate the recognized problem to the front cockpit and continued toward an altitude that had been read back incorrectly. The CRM concept was not applied to the analysis of the situation at the point where the error could still have been trapped. The result was that the IP had to intervene, restate the clearance and execute part of the corrective action. SP was unable to reconstruct the breakdown during the debriefing without IP assistance.

SP, due to a briefing sequence that addressed communication and airmanship only in general terms, did not highlight on the IFG/CRM matrix chart the particular items applicable to the sortie. In flight the division of radio and navigation duties was established only after the IP's verbal indications, and recognition of the workload imbalance came with delay. The CRM items were addressed and the CRM box was completed, but only with prompting and without IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to the authority gradient in the IP/SP cockpit, which suppressed an upward challenge, did not voice the recognized discrepancy between the assigned heading and the one being flown until the IP invited comment. The CRM concept was therefore applied to the analysis of the situation only after verbal indications, and the correction was made with delay. The sequence was completed without IP intervention on the controls, but the required inquiry and advocacy were not initiated by SP.

SP integrated CRM skills into the briefing, the flight and the debriefing within the desired standards for the Training Section; however, the applicable items highlighted on the IFG/CRM matrix chart were not revisited when the approach sequence changed. Coordination of cockpit duties was re-established by SP in a timely manner and without IP's intervention. Performance is marginal for the Training Section, since the rolling review of the plan lapsed twice under workload. Consistency in updating the shared picture between cockpits is expected to improve.

SP applied the CRM concept accurately and rapidly in the planning of the maneuvers and in the analysis of the simulated emergency, using the IFG/CRM matrix chart on his own initiative to highlight the applicable items. Communication between cockpits was standard and timely throughout, and the division of duties was restated without prompting when the approach clearance changed. SP demonstrated clear understanding of when CRM enhances mission performance and flight safety and solicited comments during the debriefing. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated CRM above the level expected of the Training Section, briefing the applicable matrix chart items together with the identified threats and the named decision points, and maintaining explicit role assignment throughout the instrument sortie. Under the compounded workload of the abnormal indication and the re-route, the crew coordination, the inquiry toward the IP and the plain-language statement of the aircraft condition to ATC were all maintained without degradation. The self-critique in the debriefing identified the CRM behaviours that had contributed to mission effectiveness and safety, with negligible omissions. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a mission planning method that did not integrate CRM skills into the briefing, did not brief the applicable items of the IFG/CRM matrix chart and established no division of cockpit duties for the approach and the missed approach. When the approach was changed and the workload increased, the CRM concept was not used to analyze the situation. The result was that the IP had to direct the reallocation of duties and execute part of the communication and the navigation setup. Further preparation on the CRM briefing content is required before the next sortie.

SP, due to workload management that left the approach setup unfinished before the descent, attempted aircraft control, navigation and communication simultaneously and shed no secondary task when the workload increased. The recognized problem was not communicated to the front cockpit and the CRM concept was not applied to the analysis of the situation. The result was that the IP had to take the radios and execute part of the approach setup for the mission to continue. SP could not reconstruct the sequence during the debriefing without IP assistance.

SP, due to a debriefing technique that listed events without relating them to the graded CRM items, did not identify the particular areas for CRM development and did not use the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight them. In flight the division of radio and navigation duties was set out only after the IP's verbal indications, and correction of the imbalance came with delay. All CRM items were eventually addressed and the CRM box was completed, but only with prompting and without IP intervention on the controls.

SP, due to absent inquiry when the observed aircraft performance did not match the expected, did not question the approach setup that was already contradicted by the navigation display and advocated no alternative once the first plan had clearly failed. The CRM concept was applied to the analysis of the situation only after the IP's verbal indications, and the recognition was delayed. The sequence was completed with prompting and without the IP executing any part of it.

SP, due to a briefing that covered mission planning and communication but did not address the airmanship subcategories applicable to the sortie, left part of the IFG/CRM matrix chart unhighlighted before the flight. In flight the division of cockpit duties was not restated when the holding clearance was issued, which SP recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. The CRM items were graded and discussed in full during the debriefing.

SP, due to absent verbalisation of the aircraft state, so that distributed situational awareness was not maintained, did not keep the front and rear cockpit assessments consolidated during the transition to the approach. The omission was minor and SP re-established the shared picture with a timely statement of position and intentions, without IP's intervention. Areas for CRM development were identified by SP during the debriefing and the CRM box was completed without prompting.

SP integrated CRM skills into the briefing, the flight and the debriefing accurately and with adequate proficiency, using the IFG/CRM matrix chart to highlight the applicable items without prompting. Cockpit duties were divided before departure and restated at each phase change, and the CRM concept was applied when the simulated emergency was analyzed. Performance is at the desired standard but marginal, since the shared picture between cockpits was rebuilt slowly on the first workload increase. Timeliness of crew coordination under increasing workload is expected to improve over the remaining instrument sorties.

SP demonstrated exceptional CRM across all three conditions of the item, briefing the applicable matrix chart items together with the identified threats, the divert criteria and the named decision points before engine start. Throughout the instrument sortie the explicit role assignment, the cross-cockpit statement of the aircraft state and the standard phraseology with ATC were maintained without degradation under the workload of the abnormal indication and the unplanned approach change. In the debriefing SP identified his own areas for CRM development and the points at which crew coordination enhanced mission effectiveness and safety, with negligible omissions. Above end of block MIF achieved.
